html:
Coffee became the main export of Colombia in the late 1800s and stayed so for most of the 1900s. Much of it was grown on small family farms in the mountains of Antioquia, Caldas and their neighbours.

Settlers from Antioquia moved south through the forests of the central Andes in the 1800s, clearing land and founding towns such as Manizales. Coffee suited these steep, mild slopes. In 1927 the growers founded the National Federation of Coffee Growers, which bought crops, built roads and schools and later created the advertising figure Juan Valdez.

Coffee paid for railways and cities and tied Colombia to world markets. Price falls helped bring on the Thousand Days' War and the troubles of the 1930s. The Coffee Cultural Landscape became a World Heritage Site in 2011. The story parallels Brazil, on a smaller and more equal scale.
